conviction_note: Two large opposing forces that I sized separately and netted: the headline growth the market rewarded in June is 84% one undisclosed line item that already fell 34% sequentially (negative, -1.6), reinforced by an industry take-rate read-through and a finance-leadership vacuum (-0.7, -0.6), against a near-certain capital-return renewal because the US$50m buyback authorisation expires 2026-09-09, the day after the print (+1.8), and a small negative for the NYSE sub-$1 asymmetry (-0.3); the sum is -1.4, deliberately inside this name's 1.73% median reaction because with no options, 254k ADS/day of volume and no live sell-side note the price mechanism here expresses information slowly rather than violently.

findings.finding: Waterdrop's entire revenue growth story is one line: technical service income went RMB1.8m (Q4 2024) to RMB9.4m (Q1 2025) to RMB639.6m (Q4 2025) to RMB421.0m (Q1 2026) -- so it already fell 34.2% sequentially in Q1 2026 -- while brokerage income, the actual insurance business, was RMB648.6m / RMB670.8m / RMB724.8m over the same span, i.e. +11.7% YoY against the +64.8% headline, with sales and marketing rising from 22.9% to 43.6% of revenue and net profit falling to RMB98.4m from RMB108.2m.
findings.why_not_priced: The decomposition requires subtracting the disclosed technical service line out of 'insurance-related income' -- a subtraction no aggregator performs, because every wire, Chinese and English, reprints the two headline numbers (+64.8% revenue, +74.1% insurance-related income) and stops. If the market had done the arithmetic, the last print on 2026-06-17 would not have paid +2.34% for a quarter in which net profit fell 9.1% YoY and the sole growth engine turned down 34% QoQ; there would be a published EPS consensus (there is none), and the only sell-side note on the tape would not be a UOB Kay Hian buy at US$2.20 dated 2025-03-14 (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/WDH/waterdrop-inc-receives-a-buy-rating-from-uob-kay-hian-with-price-lcl1sqnsy0x3.html), eighteen months stale and citing FY2024 net profit growth of 119.8%. The company has never disclosed the composition or counterparties of the line; its stated definition includes 'marketing services to insurance companies, insurance brokers, and agency companies', i.e. a gross-up of resold traffic, which is exactly why S&M rose 213.8% for 5.3% more operating profit.
findings.independence: Two separate Chinese outlets reached the same conclusion from the same disclosure without the QoQ inflection: Sina Finance, 2026-03-27, flagged the 354x jump to RMB639.6m and that it is 48.82% of insurance-related income with the composition and buyers undisclosed (https://finance.sina.com.cn/roll/2026-03-27/doc-inhsmnzp9505963.shtml), and Tencent News, 2026-04-11, argued the company 'spends more than one yuan to generate one yuan in revenue growth' (https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260411A07DEQ00). The Q4 2025 RMB639.6m and the S&M/operating-profit series are cross-checked against the company's own Q4 exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000110465926034227/tm269697d1_ex99-1.htm) and the Q2 2025 release, whose RMB97.3m operating profit matches my FY-minus-quarters derivation exactly. Note this finding and the Huize finding below point the same direction but rest on different documents and different mechanisms.
findings.source_cluster_note: Shares the Q1 2026 exhibit with no other finding in this file.

findings.finding: Huize Holding, the closest listed Chinese online life/health insurance brokerage, reported H1 2026 on 2026-08-20 with gross written premium +29.8% and first-year premium +48.7% but operating revenue up only 5.8% -- revenue per unit of premium fell from 21.1% to 17.2%, an 18.5% relative collapse in the channel take rate, in exactly the April-June window Waterdrop is about to report.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a different ticker's release, published on 2026-08-20 -- after Waterdrop last spoke about its business (2026-06-16) and before the 2026-08-25 date announcement -- and the coverage of it (TipRanks: 'Record Premiums and Profit Surge') read the premium and profit headlines, not the revenue-to-premium ratio. Nothing connects it to WDH: there is no shared analyst, no sector note, and WDH's 20d run-up is +2.0%, i.e. the tape did not move on 2026-08-20. If the read-through were priced, WDH would have traded down that week rather than sitting pinned at $0.99-$1.00.
findings.independence: Waterdrop's own numbers point the same way from a different document: brokerage income of RMB724.8m in Q1 2026 on FYP that grew 80.2% YoY as of Q2 2025 implies the same take-rate compression (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001823986/000110465926074836/tm2618160d1_ex99-1.htm). Directionally overlapping with finding 1 -- treat as partially redundant, which is why it is sized at under half of it.

findings.finding: Waterdrop will report Q2 2026 with no CFO (vacant since Kangping Shi left in June 2022), no head of finance (Xiaoying Xu resigned as VP of finance and head of finance effective 2026-07-31), and a replacement audit-committee financial expert who took the seat only on 2026-07-01 after Heping Feng resigned from the audit, compensation and nominating committees -- two finance-governance exits inside 30 days, both immediately after the FY2025 20-F carrying the undisclosed RMB639.6m revenue line.
findings.why_not_priced: The two events were reported separately and framed positively or neutrally by the only outlets that touched them: the director change was written up as 'Waterdrop Names New Independent Director and Audit Chair as Board Reshuffles' (TipRanks) and the finance exit as an AI-investment question by Simply Wall St (https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/insurance/nyse-wdh/waterdrop/news/what-does-waterdrops-wdh-finance-exit-reveal-about-its-ai-in). Nobody has put the two 6-Ks next to each other, or next to the fact that the top finance job has been unfilled for four years. If the cluster were priced, the 2026-07-24 session would carry a volume spike -- it does not; the stock closed $1.12 that day, mid-range, and drifted.
findings.independence: The second, separate 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000110465926076631/tm2618547d1_ex99-1.htm dated 2026-06-23, which discloses Feng's resignation from all three board committees and Chang's appointment effective 2026-07-01. Feng's designation as the audit committee financial expert is stated in the FY2025 20-F (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001823986/000110465926049772/wdh-20251231x20f.htm). Different filings, different dates, one theme -- I file it as one finding, not two.

findings.finding: The US$50 million share repurchase authorisation expires on 2026-09-09 -- the day after this print -- with the great majority unused (cumulative buybacks moved only from US$118.1m to US$120.1m between the Q4 and Q1 releases, and the 20-F puts usage under the September 2025 programme at US$9.5m as of 2026-03-31), and Waterdrop has launched a new programme in September 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 and declared a US$0.03/ADS cash dividend alongside both its Q2 2025 and Q4 2025 results.
findings.why_not_priced: The expiry date lives in one sentence of a twelve-month-old press release and appears in no calendar, no aggregator and no options market -- there is no options market on this name at all, so there is no mechanism by which a known forward event gets discounted here. A fresh authorisation of up to US$50m is roughly 11-14% of the US$366m market cap and about 190 sessions of the 254,685-ADS average volume, on a stock whose US$417.6m cash position exceeds its market cap. If this were priced, the run-in would not be +2.7% over five days off a 52-week low; a name with a near-certain buyback renewal and a ~6% annualised declared dividend yield would not be pinned at $0.99. The low end of my range is negative because the board has a live reason to skip the dividend this time: US$0.03 is 2.9% of a $1.02 spot and the ex-date would mechanically push the price under $1.00, so a dividend the holder base has come to expect could instead be cut or deferred.
findings.independence: The five-programme history is stated in a different company document, the Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000110465925117939/tm2532559d2_ex99-1.htm, 2025-12-03): 'Pursuant to the share repurchase programs launched in September 2021, September 2022, September 2023, September 2024, and September 2025'. Cumulative-spend figures come from the Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 exhibits. This finding and the NYSE finding below both bear on the same announcement decision -- collapse them if scoring by cluster.

findings.finding: WDH's NYSE Rule 802.01C 30-trading-day average closing price is $1.0263 as of 2026-09-04 (window 2026-07-27 to 2026-09-04), and the five sessions rolling out of that window closed $1.15/$1.15/$1.15/$1.14/$1.12, so the next five closes must average at least $0.984 to keep the average above $1.00 -- roughly 3.5% of cushion from the $1.02 spot, with the print the only scheduled catalyst inside that window.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a computation, not a disclosure: it requires taking 30 daily closes and averaging them, and no company release, no aggregator field and no wire story states it. The eye-catching detail in the same series is that WDH closed at exactly $1.00 for thirteen consecutive sessions (2026-08-05 to 2026-08-21) and exactly $0.99 for the six after -- a pin, not a random walk, on a $260k/day notional. If the threshold were priced, the run-in would show either accelerating decline or a squeeze, not nineteen sessions of a flat line inside a one-cent band; and there would be an English-language story on it, of which there are none. Signed slightly negative because a $1.02 stock five sessions from a non-compliance notice has a fatter left tail on a bad print -- mandates that cannot hold non-compliant names sell -- while the offsetting 'management acts to support the price' channel is already carried in the buyback finding above.
findings.independence: Two Chinese outlets flag the threshold without doing the arithmetic: China Financial Online, 2026-08-06, 'Waterdrop's share price touches the warning line' (http://sc.stock.cnfol.com/gushijujiao/20260806/32327351.shtml), and a China Business Herald report of 2026-07-25 cited there on overseas-listed insurtechs falling below the US$1 line. Shares direction with, but is arithmetically independent of, the buyback finding; the price series is a different source from any company filing.

searched_and_found_nothing: The sweep's lead hypothesis -- an NFRA commission-cap or 'reporting and execution consistency' (bao xing he yi) enforcement action landing in the April-June 2026 quarter -- does not hold. The non-auto bao xing he yi regime took effect 2025-11-01 (http://www.news.cn/20251010/b8bbcefb0f3741889df474ed601f316b/c.html), and the regulator's unifying Q&A of January 2026 explicitly exempts short-term accident and health insurance, which is Waterdrop's fastest-growing FYP category (https://www.cnfin.com/hb-lb/detail/20260109/4362793_1.html). The one Q2-adjacent requirement, real-time settlement for high-frequency internet-scenario business, starts 2026-07-01, i.e. Q3 not Q2. No Q2 regulatory shock; if anything the exemption is why Waterdrop could push volume so hard.

An administrative penalty against the brokerage entity (Baoduoduo / Waterdrop Insurance Brokerage) in 2026 -- searched the NFRA and PBoC penalty disclosure lists and Chinese financial press; found nothing naming the subsidiary.

An apparent RMB368m fall in the stated cash position between 2025-12-31 and 2026-03-31 looked like a cash burn against reported profit, but restricted cash rose RMB287m over the same balance sheet and total liabilities rose RMB588m, so it is premium float moving between line items, not burn. Dropped rather than filed.
A pending ADS ratio change or reverse split -- no announcement, no 6-K, nothing on the IR site.

First-year premium (FYP) for Q1 2026 -- the company disclosed FYP in the Q2 2025 release (RMB3,204.3m, +80.2%) but stopped giving a group FYP figure in the Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 releases, so the operating-cost-to-FYP ratio the sweep wanted cannot be computed for the current quarter. The omission itself is suggestive but I could not source it to anything beyond the absence.
Huimin / E-Find digital clinical trials as a swing factor -- it is RMB24.2m of RMB1,242.2m revenue growing 5.4% YoY; too small to move a print however it lands.

Any Form 4 or insider transaction cluster (foreign private issuer, so no Section 16 filings exist), and any current sell-side estimate revision on the name -- the newest broker note I could date is 2025-03-14.
baseline_tension: There is no skew and no implied move to agree or disagree with, so the only baseline statement is the tape: a stock 48.7% off its high, 4.8% off its low, pinned at $0.99-$1.02 for a month with a +2.7% five-day bounce into the print -- and my findings cut both ways against it, because the margin and revenue-quality work agrees with the year-long derating and is therefore partly priced, while the buyback expiring the day after the print and the 30-day-average arithmetic are forward mechanical facts that a $260k/day tape with no options has no way to have discounted; the amended baseline is right that this name has essentially never reacted to a print, and that is the reason I capped a genuinely eventful setup at -1.4 rather than sizing it to the fundamentals.
